subject: Priority throughput pledge review — EonHealth
messages:
From: Sara Hughes <sara.hughes@eonhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonathan Li <jonathan.li@eonhealth.com>
Date: 2028-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Priority throughput pledge for clinical batch window

Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and cost numbers looked promising. We have an internal ask from operations: during our daily clinical ingestion window (02:00–04:00 PT) we need a predictable throughput floor for critical inference pipelines. Can Redwood provide a short-term "priority throughput pledge" that guarantees sustained throughput for that 2-hour window for our pilot?

Key constraints:
- Expected sustained throughput: ~250 requests/sec for the 2-hour window (models are 8k tokens avg).
- Target 95th-percentile latency: <= 300ms for the majority of requests (we know some long tails exist).
- Data residency: remains within us-west region.

Sara
Sara Hughes
Head of Clinical Integrations, EonHealth
Sara.Hughes@eonhealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Hughes <sara.hughes@eonhealth.com>
Cc: Jonathan Li <jonathan.li@eonhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Priority throughput pledge for clinical batch window

Sara — appreciate the clear constraints. We can propose a plan but will need quick confirmation from product and ops on feasibility and on what level of contractual commitment legal can support.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Internal feasibility check (Dylan + Ops): can we guarantee sustained 250 rps for a 2-hour window in us-west without violating other SLAs? If not, propose a graduated pledge (e.g., 200 rps guaranteed + burst buffer) and fallback model variants.
2) Operational runbook (Marissa): provide runbook for the window, on-call rotation, and prewarming steps.
3) Legal language (Lauren): share suggested pledge wording and any carveouts for force majeure, abuse, or sustained multi-customer spikes.
4) Send customer-facing pledge draft + runbook for Eon signoff.

Im looping everyone — please reply with feasibility and a single recommended pledge (exact numbers + failure modes) by end of day tomorrow so I can put a short proposal back to Eon. Attaching the Eon draft I started.

Attachment: eon_priority_pledge_draft_v2.pdf (1 page)

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Hughes <sara.hughes@eonhealth.com>, Jonathan Li <jonathan.li@eonhealth.com>
Date: 2028-08-30T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Priority throughput pledge for clinical batch window

Karthik / team —

Operational notes from CS and SRE perspective: 
- Prewarming: we will need a 30–45 minute prewarm with synthetic traffic to populate KV caches and ensure model resides on GPU nodes. Plan to schedule prewarm at 01:15 PT for the 02:00 start.
- Autoscale/Burst: recommend a dedicated reserved pool for the 2-hour window (to avoid noisy neighbor impact). If customer signs a 3-month reserved capacity commitment for the peak window, we can offer a stronger pledge.
- Monitoring/Runbook: Ive drafted a short runbook (attached) that covers escalation (pager routing), automatic fallback to a compatible quantized model variant, and a manual rollback to lower throughput mode.

Attachment: operational_runbook_eon.xlsx (runbook + escalation matrix)

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Hughes <sara.hughes@eonhealth.com>, Jonathan Li <jonathan.li@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-31T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Priority throughput pledge for clinical batch window

Quick technical feasibility:
- Sustained 250 rps for 8k-token-average requests is heavy but achievable if we provision a reserved GPU pool with autoscale headroom. Estimated required capacity: 6 x A100-class instances (quantized model runtime) with continuous batching optimizations.
- Latency target: p95 ~ 250–320ms is realistic in an isolated pool; p99 will be higher. We should avoid committing to p99 for this initial pledge.
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to an economical quantized variant will lower latency variance and cost, but output quality differences must be accepted by Eon for fallback windows.

Recommendation (single pledge):
- Guaranteed sustained throughput: 200 rps reserved capacity + guaranteed burst to 260 rps (subject to 15 min prewarm and operational runbook).
- p95 latency target: <= 300ms; explicit carveout that occasional p99 spikes may exceed 1s under load or during headroom scaling.
- Duration: pilot pledge for 90 days with metrics review and option to convert to reserved commit.

If that sounds acceptable to legal and CS we can present to Eon as a firm proposal.

Dylan Brooks
Product Manager, Serving Runtime
dylan_brooks@redwood.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Sara Hughes <sara.hughes@eonhealth.com>
Date: 2028-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Priority throughput pledge for clinical batch window

Thanks — drafting contract language. A few legal points to flag before we send to Eon: 
- Avoid absolute uptime/latency promises: change "guaranteed burst to 260 rps" to "operationally-diligent commitment to provision burst capacity up to 260 rps subject to available capacity and prewarming".
- Add explicit carveouts: third-party cloud outages, customer-triggered traffic abuse, and emergency maintenance.
- Remedies: propose service credit structure tied to missed p95 targets (capped and time-limited), rather than termination rights.

I will attach a redline of Karthik's draft with suggested wording and a short amendment template for the pilot. Please review by 3pm PT and let me know any commercial objections.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Hughes <sara.hughes@eonhealth.com>, Jonathan Li <jonathan.li@eonhealth.com>, Procurement <procure@eonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-01T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Priority throughput pledge proposal — EonHealth pilot (90 days)

Hi Sara / Jonathan / procurement team —

Thanks for the patience. Below is a concise proposal based on internal feasibility and legal review. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk through.

Summary (90-day pilot):
- Reserved baseline: guaranteed sustained capacity for 200 requests/sec during the daily 02:00–04:00 PT window.
- Burst headroom: operational commitment to provision burst capacity up to 260 requests/sec following a 30–45 minute prewarm. Burst subject to available reserved pool and normal carveouts.
- Latency commitment: p95 latency target <= 300ms across the window. Explicit carveout that occasional p99 spikes may exceed 1s during scaling or exceptional conditions.
- Operational controls: prewarm at 01:15 PT, dedicated reserved pool for window, runbook and on-call escalation (see attached runbook).
- Commercial: pilot priced as month-to-month for 90 days; conversion to a reserved capacity commit (3 mo minimum) will be discussed at the review call.

Attachments: eon_priority_pledge_draft_v2.pdf, operational_runbook_eon.xlsx

Next steps: please confirm acceptance of the above terms or propose edits by end of week. If accepted, Lauren will send a short amendment for signatures and Marissa will schedule the prewarm and the runbook dry-run with SRE.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
